newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks break resistance, end 2.77pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks break resistance, end 2.77pct higher.

text.p: Greek stocks jumped 2.77 percent on Monday breaking the 1,200 resistance level on strong volume, boosted by a good 6.8 percent January inflation figure and a temporary pause in the farmers' strike.

"An important factor that sent the market to explosive highs on Monday was the announcement on Friday of a drop in inflation to 6.8 percent. This number exceeded our most optimistic expectations," said broker Iakovos Diamantopoulos at Hermes Brokerage.
Another factor was the end of the recent crisis between farmers and the Greek government as farmers decided to temporarily pull back their tractors on Sunday.
On Friday, National Bank announced a 0.25 percent interest rate cut on savings deposits, which further boosted equities on Monday, he added.

"The 1,200 level was broken on high volume, with strong buying interest across-the-board. I consider 1,200 points to have become a support level and I expect the new resistance level at 1,300 points," Diamantopoulos said.

The market can only move upwards as investors' reservations concerning the recent rise, which was based solely on rallying blue-chips, have been abandoned and buying interest is focused on medium and small caps of all sectors, he added.
The Athens general share index finished 2.77 percent or 32.89 points hihger at 1220.69 points from Friday's 1187.80, after opening at 1192.24.
Gainers led losers 202 to 30 with 16 issues unchanged on 248 traded. Turnover was 18.6 billion drachmas on volume of 7.0 million shares.
All sectoral indices rallied with leasing shares leading the climb with a 4.17 percent rise followed by construction shares up 3.99 percent.
Banks rose 3.52 percent, insurance shares gained 3.36 percent, industrials ended 2.33 percent higher and small caps closed up 2.78 percent.
